title: 4-round AES-192: Birthday bottleneck distinguisher

target.description: AES-192 on 128-bit blocks. Consecutive inner rounds each include MixColumns; the round keys are fixed and unknown. The source explicitly specifies left-going ShiftRows.

setting.key_relation: Four fixed, unknown 128-bit round keys. The structural argument does not use their master-key dependencies, and therefore also applies to keys derived from any of the standard AES key lengths.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: About2^16 distinct c triplets and16 distinct y values for each, holding the other twelve input bytes fixed.
assumptions: The four c-dependent byte parameters are modeled as a random32-bit function of c. Equality on16 sampled y values is assumed to give negligible false alarms.
setting.reference_model: Chosen-input access to four fixed-key inner rounds is compared with a uniformly random permutation on 128-bit blocks, using the same input structures and projected output tests.

time.note: Printed p.21 gives strictly less than2^20 reference AES executions, in the author's accounting. No calibration to a full standard AES implementation is applied.

data.note: About 2^16 choices of c times sixteen y values; these are inputs to the four-round component.

memory.reported: Lists of sixteen projected bytes for each selected c; peak not itemized
memory.note: The collision detector forms and compares the projected output lists. The paper does not state a complete peak-storage count.

preprocessing.note: The paper does not separately price setup for this endpoint.

success.description: The author gives about one-half probability of finding a function collision by the birthday argument. This is not a numerically derived total distinguishing advantage or a measured software success frequency.

evidence.interpretation: Version-specific primary text; printed pagination retained for each inspected copy.

limitations: Primary-text claims are catalogued by target and scope. Full attacks, cost estimates and global success are not independently reproduced.
